pr.author: scottmcm

processing.reason: The PR is a rejection/validation change, not a value-level miscompilation. The removed codegen branch lowered `a.0` for power-of-two `#[repr(simd)]` newtypes via alloca/store/load; because it asserted `field.size == self.layout.size`, that lowering is exactly a same-size bit reinterpretation and produces the same bits as the supported `mem::transmute`/raw-pointer cast. Non-power-of-two SIMD already took the old `bug!` branch (the workaround required `count.is_power_of_two()`), and `repr(simd, packed)` types of differing size likewise did not use this value-correct path. The actual historical difference is that the Validator now emits broken-MIR `Projecting into SIMD type ... is banned by MCP#838` and codegen reaches `span_bug!`, i.e. compile failure/ICE versus successful compilation, not different defined runtime values. Therefore no source-grounded original/transformed function pair exists that both pass Miri and produce different observable values; manufacturing one (e.g. changing the return value or an unrelated rewrite) would not encode the PR's actual wrong transformation. The regression is correctly represented by the PR's `build-fail` UI test, not by `test_program_pair`.

evidence: "Projecting into SIMD type {adt_def:?} is banned by MCP#838"
"Non-ref type {self:?} cannot project to ref field type {field:?}"
// It would be nice to just ban `.0` into simd types,
//! Historically the tests just made their own, but projections into simd types
//~| ERROR Projecting into SIMD type U32x4 is banned by MCP#838
// Newtype vector of array, e.g. #[repr(simd)] struct S([i32; 4]);
// This was originally just `a.0`, but that ended up being annoying enough
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation/behavior was treating a projection into a SIMD newtype's field (e.g. `a.0` where `a: #[repr(simd)] struct U32x4([u32; 4])`) as legal MIR and lowering it through the alloca/store/load workaround. This PR's fix declares such a projection invalid in the Validator and removes the codegen workaround. Concretely, instead of accepting the projection, the Validator emits `"Projecting into SIMD type {adt_def:?} is banned by MCP#838"`, and codegen's branch now calls `span_bug!` with `"Non-ref type {self:?} cannot project to ref field type {field:?}"`. This is not an optimization rewrite: the two comparable programs differ only in whether the SIMD-to-array conversion is written as a `.0` projection (rejected) or as a transmute/raw-pointer reinterpretation (accepted).
analysis.inputDomain: MIR/place projections where the parent type is an ADT with `adt_def.repr().simd()`, arising from Rust source field access into a `#[repr(simd)]` or `#[repr(simd, packed)]` newtype (e.g. `a.0`, destructuring `let f32x4([a0,a1,a2,a3]) = ...`, or `derive(Clone)`/`derive(PartialEq)`/`derive(Debug)` on such a type). The input domain includes power-of-two and non-power-of-two SIMD types, generic `Simd<T, const N: usize>`, and `packed` SIMD. Constructing the SIMD value directly (e.g. `i8x2::from_array([32, 64])` or `Simd([..])`) remains legal; only projecting into its field is banned.
analysis.originalLogic: Before this PR, the Validator's place-projection check handled ADT field projections without any SIMD restriction. For codegen, `OperandRef::project_field` in `compiler/rustc_codegen_ssa/src/mir/operand.rs` had a special case: when the aggregate's `BackendRepr` was `SimdVector { count, .. }`, the field was `BackendRepr::Memory { sized: true }`, and `count.is_power_of_two()`, it asserted `field.size == self.layout.size`, allocated a field place with `PlaceRef::alloca(bx, field)`, stored `self.val` into it, and then returned `bx.load_operand(place)`. The rationale in the source was: `// This is being deprecated, but for now stdarch still needs it for` `// Newtype vector of array, e.g. #[repr(simd)] struct S([i32; 4]);`.
pitfalls: `#[repr(simd)]` field access is banned even though the field may be `pub`; constructing `Simd([..])` / `from_array` and reading via raw pointer cast or transmute are the supported replacements.

`derive(Clone)`, `derive(PartialEq)`, and `derive(Debug)` on a SIMD newtype generate field projections, so they break; `tests/auxiliary/minisimd.rs` therefore defines manual impls using `as_array`/`into_array` raw-pointer casts. The auxiliary file explains that the projection ban `breaks derive(Clone)`.

Do not conflate this with the old codegen bug/assertion: the removed branch included `assert_eq!(field.size, self.layout.size)` and an alloca/store/load; the corrected behavior is to reject the projection in validation rather than reproduce that lowering.
The Validator check is inserted before the ADT variant/field lookup, so any field projection on a SIMD ADT is rejected by the MCP rule.
Non-power-of-two and `packed` SIMD types are also affected; tests such as `PackedSimd<i32, 3>` use `from_array`/`into_array` instead of `.0`.
The test expectation text is `Projecting into SIMD type U32x4 is banned by MCP#838`; the diagnostic is emitted as broken MIR.
preconditions: The projected-from type is an ADT declared with `repr(simd)` (or `repr(simd, packed)`), so `adt_def.repr().simd()` is true.
The MIR contains a field projection into that SIMD type, not merely construction of the SIMD value.
The Validator must be running on the generated MIR; the new regression test is a `build-fail` test with `failure-status: 101` and `dont-check-compiler-stderr`.
Codegen should no longer have the deprecated power-of-two SIMD-to-memory-field alloca workaround; the old special case is removed.
analysis.summary: MCP#838 bans projecting into `#[repr(simd)]` ADTs. The MIR Validator now rejects any field projection whose parent ADT has `repr().simd()`, and the codegen fallback that materialized such projections via alloca/store/load is replaced by `span_bug!`. The historical behavior was to accept and codegen these projections; tests were updated to use `mem::transmute`/raw-pointer casts and a shared `minisimd` helper instead of `.0` projections (notably because `derive(Clone)` projects into the SIMD field).
analysis.testStrategy: Add a focused MIR-validation UI test (the PR adds `tests/ui/mir/validate/project-into-simd.rs`) with `//@ build-fail`, `//@ failure-status: 101`, `//@ dont-check-compiler-stderr`, a `#[repr(simd)] pub struct U32x4([u32; 4]);`, and `pub fn f(a: U32x4) -> [u32; 4] { a.0 }`, expecting both `ERROR broken MIR in Item` and `ERROR Projecting into SIMD type U32x4 is banned by MCP#838`. Pair it with a control program that differs only in the conversion: use `unsafe { std::mem::transmute(a) }` (as in updated `tests/ui/simd/issue-105439.rs`) or a raw-pointer cast dereference (as in updated `minisimd::as_array`), which should compile and behave identically. Also cover `#[repr(simd, packed)]` non-power-of-two types and generic `Simd<T, N>`; for run-pass behavior, use `from_array`/`as_array`/`into_array` helpers rather than `.0` projections.
analysis.trigger: A `PlaceElem::Field` projection (or an equivalent field place) whose parent ADT has a SIMD representation, i.e. the newly added `if adt_def.repr().simd() { self.fail(...) }` path in the Validator type checker.
